tasks.prompt: Order the steps for exercising a gate valve on a routine round in a prairie town system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The valve must be left in its recorded normal position.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one in service gate valve, from arrival at the valve box to the completed record.

cards.label: Locate the valve using the system map and work order, and record its as found position
Open the valve box and clear out debris, water and ice
Inspect the stem, operating nut and box for damage or corrosion
Operate the valve slowly through its full travel, counting the turns
Return the valve to its recorded normal position
Record turns, direction, condition and any deficiency in the valve log

tasks.explanation: Exercising starts from the map and as found position so the valve can be restored exactly. The box is cleared and inspected before operation, the valve is cycled slowly while counting turns, returned to normal, and the visit is documented.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for opening a gate valve to restore flow after a main repair is complete.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The repair crew confirms the repair and flushing are finished.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one closed gate valve feeding the repaired section, from confirmation to full restoration.

cards.label: Confirm the repair is complete and the section has been flushed
Check the position of the downstream valves that feed the section
Open the valve one turn and pause so the section fills slowly
Continue opening slowly, counting turns, while watching for leaks at the repair
Open the valve fully, then back it off a quarter turn
Verify restored pressure and check the valve gland for leaks

tasks.explanation: The valve is opened only after repair and flushing are confirmed. Filling slowly first limits surge and air problems, the valve is then opened fully and backed off slightly so it does not seize open, and pressure and gland condition are verified last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for closing valves to isolate a section of main for a planned repair.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The repair is planned and affected customers can be notified in advance under provincial drinking water requirements.
tasks.configuration: Scope: isolation of one main section using the nearest valves on each side.

cards.label: Identify the isolation valves from the system map
Notify dispatch and the affected customers of the planned shutoff
Close the nearest upstream valve slowly
Close the nearest downstream valve slowly
Confirm isolation by checking that pressure in the section has dropped
Tag the closed valves and record the closure times

tasks.explanation: The correct valves come from the map first, customers are warned before water is shut off, the section is closed slowly to limit water hammer, isolation is proven by the pressure drop, and tagged valves plus recorded times protect the crew and the record.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for operating a gearbox butterfly valve to the fully closed position.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The butterfly valve has a geared operator with a position indicator.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one butterfly valve in a chamber, from inspection to recorded closure.

cards.label: Check the position indicator and note the starting position
Inspect the handwheel, gearbox and stem for damage
Turn the handwheel slowly in the closing direction, watching the indicator move
Stop turning when the indicator shows fully closed
Record the final position and the number of handwheel turns

tasks.explanation: The starting position is noted before anything moves, the operator is inspected, the geared handwheel is turned slowly while the indicator is watched, turning stops at the fully closed indication to avoid over torquing the disc, and the result is recorded.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for replacing a damaged valve box top section after road work buried it.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Traffic control is in place and utility locates are complete.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one buried valve box, from locating the valve to confirming access works.

cards.label: Locate and mark the valve position from the system map and a metal detector
Excavate around the box down to the damaged top section
Remove the damaged top section of the box
Set the new top section to finished road grade
Backfill and compact around the box
Insert the valve key and operate the valve to confirm access

tasks.explanation: The valve must be found before digging, the box is exposed before the damaged section can come off, the new section is set to grade before backfilling, and the job is complete only once a key proves the valve can actually be operated.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for exercising a normally closed boundary valve between two pressure zones.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The boundary valve is normally closed and must be left closed.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one normally closed zone boundary valve during a scheduled exercising round.

cards.label: Record the as found position as closed before touching the valve
Open the valve slowly through its full travel, counting turns
Close the valve slowly through its full travel, counting turns
Leave the valve fully closed, matching its as found position
Log the turn counts and report any difference between opening and closing counts

tasks.explanation: A boundary valve is exercised by cycling it fully open and fully closed, comparing turn counts to catch a broken stem, and it must be left in its normal closed position so the pressure zones stay separated.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for inspecting an automatic air release valve at a high point in the system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The air valve sits in a chamber on an isolating service valve.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one air release valve, from chamber checks to return to service.

cards.label: Open the chamber and check for standing water or damage
Close the isolating valve below the air valve
Remove the air valve cover and inspect the float and seat, clearing any debris
Reassemble the air valve and replace the cover
Open the isolating valve slowly and check for leaks and proper air release

tasks.explanation: The chamber is checked first, the isolating valve makes the air valve safe to open, the float and seat are inspected and cleaned, the valve is reassembled, and only then is the isolating valve reopened slowly and checked.

tasks.prompt: Order the troubleshooting steps when a gate valve will not fully stop flow to a work area.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. A closed gate valve is passing water into an isolated section.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one passing gate valve, from first check to the recorded outcome.

cards.label: Operate the valve to the fully closed position and confirm the turn count
Check downstream pressure to confirm water is still passing
Cycle the valve open and closed several times to flush debris off the seat
Close the valve again and recheck the downstream pressure
If it still passes, record the deficiency and schedule the valve for repair or replacement

tasks.explanation: Debris on the seat is the common cause of a passing valve, so the valve is proven closed, the leak past it is confirmed, cycling flushes the seat, the check is repeated, and only a valve that still passes is written up for repair.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a routine check of a pressure reducing valve station.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Gauges are fitted upstream and downstream of the valve.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one pressure reducing valve holding a lower zone below a higher zone.

cards.label: Record the upstream pressure at the station gauge
Record the downstream pressure and compare it with the setpoint
Check the strainer and pilot lines for blockage or leaks
Watch the downstream pressure as demand changes to confirm the valve holds the setpoint
Record both pressures and report any drift from the setpoint

tasks.explanation: Upstream pressure sets the context, downstream pressure is compared with the setpoint, the strainer and pilots are checked because they cause most drift, holding under changing demand proves control, and the readings are recorded.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for an emergency valve closure after a main break floods a street.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The break location is reported by the public and confirmed on arrival.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the first isolation of a broken main section during an emergency call out.

cards.label: Confirm the break location and identify the isolation valves on the system map
Notify dispatch of the break and the planned isolation
Close the nearest upstream valve slowly
Close the nearest downstream valve slowly
Confirm flow at the break has stopped or dropped to a safe level
Tag the valves and record the times for the break report

tasks.explanation: In an emergency the valves still come from the map, dispatch is told before isolation so customer calls can be answered, slow closure limits hammer, stopping the flow is confirmed at the break, and tagging plus times complete the record.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for the spring thaw watch on services and mains that froze during winter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Frost is leaving the ground and frozen services often thaw unevenly.
tasks.configuration: Scope: daily monitoring during the first warm week after a deep freeze winter.

cards.label: List the addresses and sections that froze during the winter
Check in with the highest risk addresses for restored or lost flow
Watch for new leaks as thawing pipes and shifting soil stress joints
Prioritize any break response in the thaw areas and protect excavations from slumping soil
Close the winter file with the final counts of frozen services and breaks

tasks.explanation: The winter list focuses the watch, address checks catch late freezes, thaw related leaks are expected rather than surprising, slumping soil changes excavation safety, and closing the file turns the winter into next years plan.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for placing a newly installed gate valve into service on a new main.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Pressure testing and disinfection of the new main are complete and accepted.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one new gate valve, from final inspection to the completed record.

cards.label: Inspect the valve, box alignment and operating nut
Operate the valve through its full travel and count the turns
Set the valve to its required normal position
Check the gland and box for leaks under full pressure
Record the valve data, including make, size, turns and normal position
Update the system map and valve inventory

tasks.explanation: The valve is inspected and proven operable before it is trusted, set to its normal position, checked for leaks under pressure, and only then entered in the records and map so future crews can find and use it.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps when a gate valve will not turn during an exercising visit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The operator has a standard valve key and no powered actuator on site.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one seized gate valve found during a routine exercising round.

cards.label: Stop applying force before the stem or nut is damaged
Check for a buried, bent or debris filled box that is blocking the key
Apply penetrating lubricant to the nut and allow it to soak
Try gentle rocking with the key, without forcing past resistance
If the valve still will not move, record it as inoperable and raise a work order
Flag the valve on the isolation plan so crews do not rely on it

tasks.explanation: Forcing a seized valve can break the stem and turn a deficiency into an outage. Clearing the box and lubricant address the common causes, gentle rocking is the limit of field force, and an inoperable valve must be recorded and flagged so isolation plans stay honest.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a routine annual fire hydrant inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The hydrant is in service and the inspection is visual and operational.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one hydrant, from exterior check to the completed inspection record.

cards.label: Check access, paint condition and the breakaway flange from outside
Remove the caps and inspect threads, gaskets and chains
Open the hydrant fully and confirm it operates and flows
Close the hydrant and confirm the barrel drains down
Replace the caps hand tight and check the operating nut
Record the hydrant condition and any deficiencies in the hydrant log

tasks.explanation: Inspection works from the outside in: access and condition first, caps and threads next, then operation, then drainage after closing, which matters for freeze protection, and finally caps replaced and findings logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for flushing a hydrant on a dead end main.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The dead end hydrant is flushed to refresh water quality.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one dead end hydrant flush, from site setup to the recorded result.

cards.label: Set up traffic control and fit a diffuser to direct the discharge
Open the hydrant slowly until it is fully open
Flush until the discharged water runs clear
Measure and record the free chlorine residual at the hydrant
Close the hydrant slowly to avoid water hammer
Record flush duration, residual and hydrant condition

tasks.explanation: Traffic control and a diffuser protect the site before water flows. The hydrant is opened slowly, flushed until clear, sampled for residual while flowing, and closed slowly because a fast closure can cause water hammer.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a hydrant flow test using a residual hydrant and a flow hydrant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Two hydrants on the same main are used, one for pressure and one for flow.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one flow test, from static pressure to the calculated result.

cards.label: Fit a gauge to the residual hydrant and record the static pressure
Open the flow hydrant fully and let the flow stabilize
Measure the pitot pressure at the flowing hydrant
Read the residual pressure at the residual hydrant while the water is flowing
Close the flow hydrant slowly
Use the recorded static, pitot and residual pressures to calculate the available flow

tasks.explanation: Static pressure is the no flow reference, so it is recorded first. The flow hydrant is opened and allowed to stabilize, pitot pressure is taken at the flowing hydrant, residual pressure is read at the same time, the hydrant is closed slowly, and the three pressures are then used to calculate available flow.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for checking that a hydrant barrel has drained after use in cold weather.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The hydrant was used the previous day and overnight temperatures are below freezing in a British Columbia interior community.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one dry barrel hydrant, from opening a cap to the reported result.

cards.label: Remove one hydrant cap
Lower a weighted line into the barrel to measure any standing water
Pump out standing water if the drain is plugged
Report the plugged drain and flag the hydrant for repair

tasks.explanation: Standing water can only be confirmed by measuring inside the barrel. Water found above the drain means the drain is plugged, the barrel is pumped out to prevent freeze damage, and the defect is reported for repair.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for taking a damaged hydrant out of service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The hydrant was struck by a vehicle and cannot be used.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one damaged hydrant, from isolation to notification.

cards.label: Close the hydrant isolation valve to take the hydrant off the main
Place the out of service cover or tag on the hydrant
Notify dispatch and the fire department that the hydrant is out of service
Log the hydrant number, date and reason, and raise a repair work order

tasks.explanation: Isolating the hydrant makes it safe, the cover warns users at the site, the fire department must know before they plan around the hydrant, and the log entry plus work order start the repair.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for placing a newly installed hydrant into service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Installation, pressure testing and disinfection are complete and accepted.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one new hydrant, from final inspection to in service notification.

cards.label: Inspect the installation, including the breakaway flange and cap chains
Open the hydrant and flush until the water runs clear
Close the hydrant and confirm the barrel drains
Record the hydrant data, including make, size and location
Notify the fire department that the hydrant is in service

tasks.explanation: The hydrant is inspected before it is flowed, flushed clear, proven to drain so it will not freeze, entered into the records, and only then reported to the fire department as available.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps when a contractor fills a water tanker from a hydrant under a hydrant use permit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Bulk filling is only allowed with a permit, a meter and backflow protection.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one permitted tanker fill at a designated hydrant.

cards.label: Verify the contractor hydrant use permit
Connect the approved backflow preventer to the hydrant outlet
Connect the hydrant meter and record the starting reading
Open the hydrant slowly and fill the tanker
Close the hydrant and record the final meter reading for billing

tasks.explanation: The permit authorizes the use, the backflow preventer protects the main before any connection flows, the meter must be read before filling starts so the volume can be billed, and the final reading closes the record.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for replacing a damaged hydrant with a new one.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Locates and traffic control are complete and a replacement hydrant is on site.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one hydrant replacement, from notification to return to service.

cards.label: Notify dispatch and the fire department of the planned removal
Close the hydrant isolation valve
Drain the barrel and unbolt the hydrant at the breakaway flange
Set and bolt the replacement hydrant
Open the isolation valve slowly, then flush the hydrant and check for leaks
Record the new hydrant data and notify the fire department it is back in service

tasks.explanation: Users are warned before the hydrant leaves service, the isolation valve makes removal safe, the breakaway flange is the designed separation point, and the new hydrant is flushed and leak checked before records and notifications close the job.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for winterizing hydrants ahead of freeze up in a northern Alberta town.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Freeze up is expected within weeks and every hydrant must drain freely.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the fall winterizing visit for one dry barrel hydrant.

cards.label: Inspect the hydrant and operate it briefly to confirm it works
Close the hydrant and time how long the barrel takes to drain
Pump out any water that remains above the drain
Check caps, chains and the operating nut, and lubricate as needed
Mark any hydrant that does not drain for repair before freeze up
Record the winterizing result for each hydrant visited

tasks.explanation: Winterizing proves drainage while repair is still possible. A hydrant that holds water will freeze and can split the barrel, so slow draining hydrants are pumped out, marked and recorded for repair before freeze up.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for repainting and lubricating a hydrant during summer maintenance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The hydrant stays in service except during the brief operating check.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one hydrant, from surface preparation to the completed record.

cards.label: Clean rust and loose paint from the hydrant body
Check and lubricate the operating nut and cap threads
Apply primer to bare metal areas
Apply the finish coat in the system colour code
Operate the hydrant briefly to confirm the lubrication worked
Record the maintenance and the colour code used

tasks.explanation: Surface preparation must come before paint or the coating fails early. Lubrication is done while the hydrant is apart, primer protects bare metal, the finish coat restores the colour code that identifies the hydrant, and a brief operation proves the work.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for restoring access to hydrants after a major prairie snowstorm.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Fire access must be restored after a blizzard in a Saskatchewan community.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one snow buried hydrant on a priority route.

cards.label: Locate the hydrant using the marker flag and the system map
Clear snow from around the hydrant to expose the caps and operating nut
Check that the caps can be removed and the nut turns
Clear a path from the street so a pumper can connect
Report any hydrant that cannot be found or is damaged

tasks.explanation: A hydrant that cannot be found or reached is out of service in practice. Clearing exposes the working parts, a connection check proves it can be used, the pumper path completes access, and missing or damaged hydrants are reported the same day.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for repairing a hydrant that leaks from the top bonnet when operated.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Spare seals and gaskets for the hydrant model are on the truck.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one hydrant with a bonnet leak, from isolation to return to service.

cards.label: Close the hydrant isolation valve and drain the barrel
Remove the bonnet and inspect the stem seals and gaskets
Replace the worn seals and gaskets
Reassemble the bonnet and open the isolation valve slowly
Operate the hydrant and check the bonnet for leaks under pressure
Close the hydrant, confirm drainage, and record the repair

tasks.explanation: The hydrant must be isolated and drained before the bonnet comes off. Seals are replaced, not just tightened, the valve is restored slowly, and the repair is proven by operating under pressure and confirming the barrel still drains.

tasks.prompt: Order the planning steps for a unidirectional flushing program for the whole system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The program cleans mains systematically rather than flushing random hydrants.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program planning, from reviewing records to issuing customer notices.

cards.label: Review the system map, complaint records and residual results
Divide the system into flushing zones that start at the clean water source and move outward
Sequence the valves and hydrants to be used in each zone
Estimate the flows needed and schedule crews and dates for each zone
Issue customer notices for the zones in the order they will be flushed

tasks.explanation: Planning starts from records so problem areas shape the zones. Unidirectional flushing always works from the clean source outward so loosened deposits are pushed ahead of clean water, never back into cleaned mains.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for carrying out unidirectional flushing in one zone.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The zone plan, valve list and customer notices are already issued.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one flushing zone, from valve setup to restoration.

cards.label: Set up traffic control at the flushing hydrant
Close the zone valves so water can enter the zone from only the planned inlet
Open the flushing hydrant fully to reach the target flushing velocity
Flush until the water runs clear and the chlorine residual meets the target
Close the hydrant and return all zone valves to their normal positions
Record the flushing volume, residual and valve positions

tasks.explanation: The zone is isolated to one inlet before the hydrant opens, which is what makes the flow unidirectional and able to reach scouring velocity. Flushing continues until clarity and residual targets are met, then valves are restored and documented.

tasks.prompt: Order the hydrant sequence when flushing a series of hydrants along one main in a flushing zone.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Three hydrants sit along the zone main, from the inlet toward the far end.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the order in which three hydrants are flushed within the zone.

cards.label: Confirm the zone valves are set as planned
Open the hydrant nearest the zone inlet and flush until clear, then close it
Open the next hydrant downstream and flush until clear, then close it
Open the hydrant at the far end of the zone and flush until clear, then close it
Restore all zone valves to their normal positions and record the results

tasks.explanation: Flushing moves from the inlet downstream so each section is cleaned with water that has only passed through already cleaned pipe. Working in reverse order would drag deposits back into finished sections.

tasks.prompt: Order the preparation steps on the morning of a unidirectional flushing day.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The zone plan exists and the work is scheduled for today.
tasks.configuration: Scope: crew preparation before the first hydrant is opened.

cards.label: Review the zone plan, valve list and target flows with the crew
Confirm the zone valves were exercised and operate ahead of the flush
Confirm customer notices for todays zone were delivered
Stage hydrant diffusers, pressure gauges and sampling equipment
Brief the crew on the hydrant order and safety setup

tasks.explanation: A stuck valve or a missed notice can stop a flushing day, so the plan is reviewed, valves are proven operable in advance, notices are confirmed, equipment is staged, and the crew briefing ties the sequence together before work starts.

tasks.prompt: Order the response when a customer reports dirty water during unidirectional flushing in their zone.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Flushing is active in the customers zone today.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one dirty water call received while flushing is under way nearby.

cards.label: Check whether the address is inside the zone being flushed today
Advise the customer to avoid using hot water until flushing in the zone is finished
Once the zone is complete, advise the customer to run a cold water tap until the water clears
If the water is still dirty after that, visit the property and check the chlorine residual

tasks.explanation: Dirty water inside an active flushing zone is expected and temporary. Keeping hot water off protects the water heater from sediment, the cold tap flush clears the service after the main is clean, and a visit is only needed if the problem outlasts the zone work.

tasks.prompt: Order the close out steps at the end of a unidirectional flushing program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. All zones in the program have been flushed.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program close out, from field data to the next cycle.

cards.label: Total the flushing volumes recorded for each zone
Compile the chlorine residual results and compare them with pre program results
Verify every program valve is confirmed back in its normal position
Report the results, problem areas and water used to the supervisor
Schedule the next program cycle and note zones needing earlier attention

tasks.explanation: Close out turns field sheets into program evidence: volumes and residuals show what the program achieved, valve positions are verified so the system is left normal, and the report drives the timing of the next cycle.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a conventional dead end flushing round on a small Manitoba system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The round follows a fixed list of dead ends with low turnover.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a monthly round covering several dead end hydrants and blow offs.

cards.label: Review the dead end list and the last residual results
Flush the dead end nearest the source first and work outward
At each point, flush until clear and measure the chlorine residual
Record the residual, flush time and any discolouration for each point
Report any point where the residual stays low after flushing

tasks.explanation: Working outward keeps clean water behind the work. Residuals measured at each point show whether flushing restored quality, and a point that stays low after flushing points to a bigger problem than stagnation, so it is reported.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for operating a main blow off at the end of a rural line.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The blow off discharges to a ditch through an air gap.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one blow off assembly in a chamber at a line end.

cards.label: Open the chamber and inspect the blow off valve and discharge line
Open the blow off valve slowly and direct the discharge safely
Flush until the water runs clear and the residual reaches the target
Close the valve slowly and confirm the chamber drains
Record the flush volume estimate and the residual result

tasks.explanation: The chamber and discharge are checked before flow starts, slow opening and closing protect the main from surge, flushing continues to clarity and residual targets, and drainage plus records complete the visit.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for flushing a main after a break repair before it returns to normal service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The repair is complete and the section has been disinfected under the utility procedure.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the repaired section, from repair completion to restored service.

cards.label: Confirm the repair is complete and the section is isolated from customers
Open the flushing hydrant at the low end of the section slowly
Flush until the water runs clear with no debris
Measure the chlorine residual and collect samples as directed
Restore the section valves to normal once results are accepted
Record the flushing and sampling results in the break report

tasks.explanation: Flushing after a repair removes debris and disinfectant before customers receive the water. Samples and residuals prove quality, valves are restored only after acceptance, and the break report carries the full record.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing a main section for an ice pigging cleaning run arranged by the utility.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. A specialist contractor supplies the ice slurry and equipment.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparation and restoration around a contractor led ice pigging run.

cards.label: Isolate the section using the planned valves and notify affected customers
Confirm the entry and exit hydrants are operable and accessible
Support the contractor as the ice slurry is pushed through the section
Flush at the exit hydrant until the water runs clear after the run
Restore the valves, measure the residual and record the cleaning result

tasks.explanation: The utility prepares isolation, access and notification, the contractor runs the slurry, and the utility flushes, checks residual and restores the section. Each party does its part in order so the section is never left isolated or unrestored.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps when routine monitoring finds a very low chlorine residual at a far end site.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The result is confirmed by a repeat test at the site.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one low residual finding at a distribution monitoring point.

cards.label: Confirm the low result with a repeat residual test
Check recent flushing, storage levels and any nearby main work
Flush the nearest hydrant or blow off until the residual recovers
Retest the residual at the monitoring point after flushing
If the residual does not recover, notify the supervisor and increase monitoring at the site

tasks.explanation: A repeat test rules out a testing error first. System checks look for the cause, targeted flushing brings in fresher water, retesting proves recovery, and failure to recover is escalated with increased monitoring rather than repeated flushing alone.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for controlling flushing discharge so it does not erode soil or enter a creek directly.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Provincial requirements protect the receiving watercourse and the utility uses dechlorination and energy dissipation.
tasks.configuration: Scope: discharge control setup at one high flow flushing hydrant near a watercourse.

cards.label: Fit a diffuser or splash plate to spread and slow the discharge
Set out dechlorination equipment for the discharge stream
Direct the flow onto a stable surface away from the creek bank
Monitor the discharge during flushing for erosion or turbidity reaching the creek
Record the discharge controls used in the flushing log

tasks.explanation: Discharge controls must be in place before high flow starts, because erosion and chlorinated water harm the receiving environment quickly. Monitoring during the flush and a log entry complete the control.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a routine external inspection of an elevated storage tank.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The inspection is done from the ground and the tank stays in service.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one elevated tank, from records review to the inspection report.

cards.label: Review the last inspection report and the tank repair history
Visually check the coating, overflow pipe, roof vent and vent screen from the ground
Check the aviation light and that the access ladder is secured
Check site drainage, fencing and the access gate
Record deficiencies and schedule the follow up work

tasks.explanation: Past reports tell the inspector what to look for. The tank shell, overflow and screened vent protect water quality, the light and ladder are safety and security items, and the site check plus written deficiencies complete the inspection.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing a storage tank for an internal inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. The tank will be drained and entered under confined space procedures.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one tank, from taking it out of service to a safe entry.

cards.label: Take the tank out of service and close and tag its inlet and outlet valves
Drain the tank down through the system or the drain line
Set up confined space controls, including ventilation and atmospheric testing
Enter and wash down the interior so surfaces can be inspected
Inspect the interior coating, roof and structure, and record the condition

tasks.explanation: Isolation and draining must come before entry, confined space controls and atmospheric testing make the entry safe, washing exposes the surfaces, and only then can the coating and structure be properly inspected.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for returning a cleaned storage tank to service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian distribution system. Cleaning and any repairs are complete and accepted.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one cleaned tank, from disinfection to normal operation.

cards.label: Disinfect the interior surfaces following the approved procedure
Fill the tank and hold the water for the required contact period
Collect bacteriological samples from the tank
Wait for satisfactory sample results before proceeding
Open the inlet and outlet valves and return the tank to service
Record the cleaning, disinfection and sample results

tasks.explanation: A cleaned tank is a new surface in contact with drinking water, so it is disinfected, filled, and proven safe by bacteriological results before its valves are opened to the system. Returning it earlier would put untested water into distribution.
